summary: Kootenai County summit: a 1931 camp, then a 40-foot L-4 tower dated 1939 (1948 in one 1996 guide), down by 1960; footings remain.

facts.design: L-4 cab on a 40-foot pole tower
facts.status_note: The tower is gone. Concrete footings, steps and debris remain on the summit.

access.note: Hike-in on Forest Service land by the Chilco Mountain National Recreation Trail.

visit.trail_note: About 1.7 miles on the Chilco Mountain National Recreation Trail to the bald summit; class 1 route.

events.note: A camp was set up on the summit; the sources give no further detail
40-foot pole tower with an L-4 cab; most sources give 1939
USGS party note that a lookout tower had been built on the peak; station benchmark under the steps
Only the 1996 Spokesman-Review guide gives 1948 for the North Chilco cabin and 40-foot tower; disputed against 1939
Ruins by 1959 per firelookout.com; climbing guide says the tower came down before 1959
USGS party referenced the legs of the lookout tower and noted it had been destroyed

evidence.supports: camp set up on the summit in 1931
evidence.quote: started in 1931 when a camp was set up on the summit

evidence.supports: 1939 40-foot pole tower with L-4 cab (Forest Lookouts page)
1948 date given by the 1996 guide, disputed
evidence.quote: North Chilco lookout cabin and 40-foot tower built in 1948; dismantled in late 1950s.

evidence.supports: 1940 USGS note: tower on the peak, benchmark under the steps
evidence.quote: 1940: a USGS party said that a lookout tower had been built on the peak and the station benchmark was under the steps and could not be used.
Sometime before 1959, the tower came down.

evidence.supports: 1960 USGS party noted the tower had been destroyed
evidence.quote: 1960 A USGS party referenced the legs of the lookout tower & that the tower had been destroyed

evidence.supports: footings, steps, cabin ruin, stovepipe and wire on the summit
evidence.quote: The ruins at North Chilco are 4 obvious cement footings, a set of cement stairs, a cement stabilizer footing, the ruins of what appears to have been a cabin, the stovepipe and lots of wire & cable.
Today you will find sparse debris from the lookout on the summit.

evidence.supports: trail is the Chilco Mountain National Recreation Trail, class 1
evidence.quote: Chilco Mountain National Recreation Trail, Class 1

evidence.supports: trail climbs 1.7 miles to the bald summit
evidence.quote: The trail climbs to the bald summit in 1.7 miles gaining 1,400 feet in elevation through a dense forest.

evidence.supports: site is in Coeur d'Alene National Forest

corrections.why: Idaho Fire Lookouts files the site as Hike-In Ruins, with footings and steps still on the summit; the ruins status describes that better than gone

notes_for_editor: Build year: 1939 in four sources (firelookout.com, Forest Lookouts, climbing guide, and the 1940 USGS note supporting a tower by then); the 1996 Spokesman-Review guide gives 1948 for the cabin and tower and says it was dismantled in late 1950s. Unresolved; the story says so. Location: the record point (47.89165, -116.5299) and idaho_fl (47.91717, -116.53062) are about 2.8 km apart; the sources here do not settle it. Height 12.2 m is from the 40-foot pole height; the sources do not give the cab height. No staffing history found in these sources, so none is recorded. Access is public hike-in per the climbing guide; the trail was not checked against 2026 Forest Service status. No new photos; the existing idahofirelookouts photo in the record still applies.
